definitions.explanation: Describes something so extreme in its unpleasantness — pain, heat, noise, boredom, sadness — that one cannot endure it. The negative potential form of {耐|た}える (to endure).

examples.japanese: この{暑|あつ}さは{耐|た}えられない。
{痛|いた}みに{耐|た}えられなくなった。
examples.english: I could no longer bear the pain.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}の{無神経|むしんけい}な{言葉|ことば}には{耐|た}えられなかった。
examples.english: I couldn't stand her insensitive words.

examples.japanese: もうこの{退屈|たいくつ}な{会議|かいぎ}には{耐|た}えられない。{早|はや}く{終|お}わってほしい。
examples.english: I can't take this boring meeting anymore. I wish it would end soon.

notes:
Negative potential form of {耐|た}える (to endure; to bear). Functions as both a predicate ({耐|た}えられない) and a modifier ({耐|た}えられない{痛|いた}み — unbearable pain). Very common in everyday speech for expressing that something exceeds one's tolerance.

The subject of what is intolerable is marked with に or には:
- {暑|あつ}さに{耐|た}えられない: can't stand the heat
- この{状況|じょうきょう}には{耐|た}えられない: can't bear this situation

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {耐|た}えられない{痛|いた}み: unbearable pain
- {耐|た}えられない{暑|あつ}さ: unbearable heat
- もう{耐|た}えられない: I can't take it anymore
- {耐|た}えられないほど: to an unbearable degree

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {我慢|がまん}できない: can't stand it — more colloquial, emphasizes the personal effort of trying to put up with something
- たまらない: unbearable; irresistible — can be negative (unbearably bad) or positive (irresistibly good)
- {堪|こた}えられない: cannot endure — literary synonym using a different kanji
